newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army charges four more in Missouri sex probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army charges four more in Missouri sex probe.

text.p: Four more noncommissioned officers at this Missouri Army base have been charged with having improper personal relationships with trainees, the Army said on Friday.
The disclosure of new charges against soldiers here was the latest development in a sexual misconduct scandal that has rocked the training base in recent days.
The charges, which range from failing to obey a lawful general regulation to indecent assault, may or may not result in trial by court martial, a spokesman at the base said.
The Army said the latest charges resulted from ongoing investigations and were not related to the unfolding rape and sexual harassment probe at Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland.

The Army spokesman said the four soldiers charged on Friday were among the 10 who had been suspended pending investigation of trainees' allegations of abuse. The spokesman said the other six soldiers were still under investigation.
The new charges were based on incidents that allegedly occurred between May and September of this year.
About 25,000 troops train at the south-central Missouri base each year, making it the second-largest of four posts where the Army conducts basic training.

Earlier this week, the Army disclosed that three drill instructors at Fort Leonard Wood had been charged with sexual misconduct. One of the men, Staff Sgt. Loren Taylor, was discharged, demoted and sentenced to confinement on Wednesday after admitting to having sex with three female recruits.
In addition to admitting to consensual sex, Taylor said he tried to have sex with a fourth recruit and had improper contact with another.
Army regulations forbid all sexual relationships between commanders and subordinates.

Three male Army trainers were charged last week in a rape and sexual harassment case involving alleged attacks on women recruits in Maryland. About 20 people were suspended from their duties at the Maryland base pending investigation.
Unlike the Maryland case, none of the Missouri cases have involved charges of rape or forcible sodomy.

With the Army checking sexual harassment complaints from female trainees at bases across the country, Defence Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday he had ordered all branches of the military to hammer home the message of "zero tolerance" for harassment of women in uniform.
